A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hair-Trigger Alignment work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–D are readable and can be matched reliably across pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama3.2-3B and Mistral-7B experiments on safety, honesty, and privacy, plus random-sequence memorization experiments measuring hidden-misalignment capacity.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds cross-step-size and multi-step safety results in Appendix D.3–D.4, Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The adversarial training objective, first-order approximation, privacy stabilization term, and LoRA capacity construction remain unchanged. The added experiments evaluate the existing fragile model under different updates without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: The alignment tasks, random-sequence task, and training/evaluation datasets are retained. Appendix D.3–D.4 reuse Alpaca and the existing Aegis2.0, AdvBench, and HarmfulQA benchmarks; their changes concern update procedures rather than data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons between original and fragile Llama3.2-3B and Mistral-7B models remain intact. Tables 6–7 evaluate the fragile Llama model against its pre-update behavior. Newly cited attacks and defenses are discussed but are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Existing protocols are retained. Appendix D.3 adds evaluation at ten step sizes from 10^-4 to 10^-3 for a model trained with update step size 10^-4. D.4 adds 1–200 updates at 10^-4 using original and disjoint Alpaca subsets. These are bounded additions for one model and task.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3–D.4 add substantive tests of two previously unanswered robustness questions: whether fragility transfers beyond the training-time step size and whether it persists through extended fine-tuning. Tables 6–7 establish persistent safety degradation under both changes, substantially extending the earlier single-step, matched-step-size analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and all existing figure results are unchanged. Tables 6–7 add safety results under different update conditions. For example, Table 7 reports AdvBench safety of 0.185 and 0.317 after 200 original/disjoint Alpaca updates, compared with 0.954 before updating. These supplement the evidence rather than revise earlier scores.

T1.justification: New Remark A.4 asserts that the construction extends to a broader class of differentiable losses, without adding a derivation. Remark A.3 explicitly identifies the frozen backbone. The existing theorems and proofs remain intact; squared loss was already specified in v1, so its newly displayed formula is clarification.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: black-box evaluation cannot guarantee post-update alignment, a single benign update can activate hidden misalignment, and hidden capacity increases with overparameterization. Additional evidence and qualifications do not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explicitly states that natural prevalence is unknown and that empirical fragile models lack the exact functional equivalence established theoretically, potentially permitting detection through further testing. It discusses benchmark-specific concealment and future exact-equivalence constructions. Section 3.3 also newly interprets retained utility results as evidence against general capability collapse explaining privacy failures.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract, whereas v1 only promises future implementation details and scripts. Appendix C remains unchanged, including that promise. The PDFs establish improved access information but do not verify repository contents or availability.

R1.justification: Section 5 materially expands positioning by identifying Gloaguen et al. (2026) as the closest work with similar adversarial meta-training behavior and distinguishing the theoretical contribution. It also adds emergent misalignment and defenses through Betley, Tamirisa, Rosati, Huang, and Qi, including discussion of adaptive attacks circumventing defenses.

P1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated limitations section and two appendix subsections while retaining the overall narrative and most existing prose. Local edits clarify static alignment terminology, change the empirical heading from 'is' to 'Can Be,' revise the abstract, and update authorship and publication information.

P2.justification: v2 adds appendix Tables 6–7 and adjusts placement of existing material, including moving Figure 3 between columns and placing Table 6 beneath Table 5. All four figure images and the existing table structures are retained; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful evidence that fragility survives mismatched step sizes and extended updates, acknowledges important limits on natural prevalence and empirical indistinguishability, and better situates closely related work. The code link improves access information. These gains are bounded: the new experiments concern one model's safety behavior, and the acknowledged gap between exact theoretical equivalence and empirical demonstrations remains unresolved.
